<p class="page-deck">A conditional, place-based scenario model for assessing co-benefits and co-costs of climate action across domestic buildings, diet and active travel. The programme separates baseline evidence, scenario action, assignment, physical or behavioural effects, causal pathways, endpoints and valuation, with explicit traceability and locality rules.</p>

**Status:** In Development  
**Relationship to the lab:** Current Lab Research — Owner-approved current programme of the Cities and Climate Learning Lab.  
**Primary theme:** [Co-benefits, co-costs and place-based valuation](/research/themes/co-benefits-place-based-valuation.html)  
**Related themes:** [Urban climate evidence infrastructure and decision-support tools](/research/themes/evidence-infrastructure-tools.html), [Climate governance and delivery modes](/research/themes/climate-governance-delivery.html)

## Research questions

- How can local climate scenarios represent co-benefits and co-costs without obscuring causal assumptions?
- How should evidence, geography and valuation choices be governed and traced?

## Scope

- **Geography:** canada, united-kingdom
- **Governance scales:** municipal, neighbourhood
- **Methods:** place-based-modelling, economic-appraisal, distributional-analysis
- **Climate domains:** mitigation
- **Sectors:** buildings, transport, health
